sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and usage
sections.what: Explains the purpose, the two usage modes, and the path it sets up for imports.
sections.why: Adds the repository root to the import path so the schema package can be found when the script runs directly.
sections.watch_out: The import line is placed after the path change on purpose, so it must not be moved above it.

sections.name: render
sections.title: Render schema
sections.what: Builds the schema text in a fixed format with a standard header and a fixed title.
sections.why: Sorting keys and fixing the indent means a real change shows in the diff and formatting changes do not.
sections.watch_out: The identifier address includes the schema version, so bumping the version changes the output.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Main entry logic
sections.what: Parses the check flag. In check mode it compares the rendered text with the file and returns an error if they differ or the file is missing. Otherwise it writes the file.
sections.why: Failing the check instead of silently rewriting lets a build catch a changed schema that was not regenerated.
sections.watch_out: The comparison is exact text, so any difference in line endings or encoding will fail the check.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Entry point
sections.what: Runs the main function when the script is started directly and passes its result on as the exit code.
sections.why: Standard way to let a command line tool report success or failure to the shell.

summary: Writes the ProcessRecord schema to a checked-in JSON file, or checks that the file is still current.
purpose: Make any change to the record contract visible in a code review diff and let an automated check catch a stale file.
why: The docstring says a checked-in file lets a reviewer see a contract change before it merges. Sorted keys and fixed indentation keep the diff free of noise.
how: The script builds the schema from the record model, adds a standard header, and renders it as sorted JSON. In check mode it compares the rendered text with the file on disk and fails if they differ. Otherwise it writes the file.
inputs: The ProcessRecord model and the schema version. An optional check flag.
outputs: A JSON schema file in the schema package, or a message and an error exit code.
risks: If the file is not regenerated after a model change, consumers outside Python will use an old contract. The header address is a fixed text string, so a version change needs that updated too.
debug: If the check fails, run the script without the flag to regenerate the file, then review the diff. If the file is missing, the check says so.
